identity: A children’s-magazine feature article in modern standard Arabic, titled سحر الشرق (“The Magic of the East”), about the Russian composer Rimsky-Korsakov and his symphony شهرزاد. The register is lyrical popular biography written for young readers: short breath-groups, heavy و/ف/ثم chaining, direct apostrophe to the reader (ولعلنا تذكرنا الآن), and rhetorical listing. Five paragraphs marked by <NL>: (1) the title strip; (2) an evocative lead on the sea, ألف ليلة وليلة and Scheherazade; (3) a single rhetorical-question paragraph, من هو إذن البحار...; (4) the biographical answer — birth, the musical family, the piano at age three, the naval academy, the professorship, then a four-movement walk-through of the symphony; (5) a two-sentence coda on his famous works and his death in 1908. It is NOT encyclopedic reference prose despite the biographical content — the voice is §F children’s magazine, not §B/§L.
law: Register first (LAW 6). I measured the opening before placing anything: this text runs at roughly 8 tokens per sentence, i.e. the §E/§F children’s band, NOT the 12–20-token §B/§L expository band that the biographical subject matter tempts me toward. Under that calibration: (a) LAW 1 at full strength — و followed by a clause carrying a NEW argument (new subject, new topic NP, heavy new PP) starts a new sentence, while و joining two nouns, two adjectives, or a bare VP sharing the subject is phrase-level and never cuts; (b) LAW 2 — ف and ثم that advance the narrative or open a new explanatory move cut, most reliably when the following verb takes a new subject; (c) LAW 1/C4 — وهي plus a nominal predicate is the single most dependable cut in this document (§L records it as my standing leak) and it fires four times; (d) LAW 4 — subordinate material that FOLLOWS its main clause stays with it (عندما, حتى, لعله, the لكن apodosis of وإن, the فقد apodosis of أما), whereas fronted adverbials attach FORWARD so the cut lands before them; (e) asyndetic topic switches (أبوه, الحركة الأولى) and new topic NPs after و (والأم, والعم, والحركة الثانية) cut, but و-joined VP chains under one shared subject weld. Net: 44 boundaries over 333 real tokens, mean segment 7.6 — exactly the rhythm the register predicts.
reasoning: SITE 22 (فيتذكر). A ف+imperfect sharing its subject inside a لما frame — my §B instinct (short result-ف welds, the @1005 false cut) fights E1 (every ف step is a sentence). Register decides: this is §E/§F, the ف-clause carries ten tokens of new content, and welding would make 15–32 a single 18-token unit against a 7.7 mean. CUT, med. SITE 28 (كتب | كتاب ألف ليلة وليلة). Appositive badal renaming the object. G2 is the precedent — gold cut خفا من الساتان ‖ أفضل خف يمكنني الحصول عليه — apposition cuts even inside otherwise welded material, and the كتب/كتاب clash at the junction is precisely where a printer sets a colon or dash. CUT, med. SITE 45 (وإن كان...صغير | لكن السيمفونية). NOT cut. C1: protasis plus apodosis is one period. The لكن here is the grammatically required answer to وإن, not a free adversative head. The same logic protects فقد at 252, the obligatory apodosis of أما — never cut a correlative in half. SITE 79 (وليلة بعد ليلة | وهي لا تكف). NOT cut. LAW 4 mirror: a fronted adverbial attaches forward, so the boundary belongs at 76 before وليلة, not at 79 after it. I placed exactly this shape one unit late in batch 1 (على ما يبدو, @1922/@1925); this time I place it early. SITE 126 (إنه الفنان ريمكسي كورساكوف | ولد في روسيا). Asyndetic, and T3 warns that mere sequence sometimes welds — but paragraph 3 is a question and this is its answer; the rhetorical closure is total. CUT, hi. SITES 132 AND 139/142 — the family sentence, where I settle T3 with a discriminator. I CUT at 132 (ولد...1844 ‖ ونشأ في أسرة فنية) because ونشأ brings a heavy new PP that opens the family topic and welding yields 21 tokens. But I do NOT cut inside تحب الموسيقى وتعشق الآلات وتعيش على أنغام. The discriminator I am adopting: ASYNDETIC parallelism cuts (LAW 3 — أنا أقوى الأقوياء ‖ أنا عظيم العظماء; يكبر ‖ يزداد طولا ‖ يتضخم), while و-JOINED chains under one shared subject weld (فجلس وأكل خبزا وشرب ماء is one segment). These three are و-joined relative verbs on أسرة فنية — subordinate, shared subject, weld. 15 tokens, my longest segment, accepted deliberately. SITE 145–147 (أنغام دو ري مي). NOT cut. Solfege reads as one quoted phrase; I put commas between them at well under 50 percent, and LAW 0 licenses cutting at a coin flip, not below one. SITE 175 (عمره | زحف). The age clause is parenthetical background sitting between ذات ليلة and the main event زحف وضرب. B5 says a comma-set parenthetical yields boundaries rather than zero. I take only the second one (before زحف) and decline the first (after ليلة at 167), because حدث أنه ذات ليلة cannot close a segment on a dangling complementizer. CUT 175, med. SITE 226 (الموهبة | لكنه واظب) — THE HARDEST SITE, a head-on collision between two of my own laws. B4 says a short لكن-clause is a TAIL: weld it and cut after (@1135 and @1690 were false cuts of mine). E1 says لكنه cuts, and cites a near-identical sentence: يعمل بجد وإخلاص ليعول أسرته ‖ لكنه كان فقيرا لا يملك أرضا ‖. Both are five-token contrastive clauses about a person, so clause length — my T2 hypothesis — does NOT separate them. Register does, which is what LAW 6 exists for: B4 was learned in §B expository running 12–20 tokens, E1 in §E narrative running 5–10, and this document measures 7.7. E1 governs. CUT, med. Logging this as the T2 test case: the discriminator is register, not length. SITE 231 (الموسيقية | وتعلم على أيدي كبار الموسيقيين الروس). Applying LAW 1’s actual test rather than the letter of و: على أيدي كبار الموسيقيين الروس introduces referents not previously in the text, so it is a new argument — unlike وزرعها (pronominal, no new argument) which rides along. CUT, med. SITE 266 (أربع حركات | أي أربعة مشاهد). أي is an explicative gloss, comma-set in print, and B5 records that a comma-set parenthetical cost me a miss. This is genuinely near 0.5, so LAW 0 breaks the tie toward cutting. CUT, lo. SITE 271 (الحركة الأولى | كانت الموسيقى). NOT cut — and this is where I deliberately refuse a LAW-0 gamble. J5/K3 (date labels, caption NPs) tempt me to split all four movement labels off their descriptions. But members three and four — والحركة الثالثة تعبر, والحركة الرابعة تعبر — are ordinary topic-comment clauses in which الحركة IS the subject of تعبر; there is no ink to reconstruct. The four members are written in parallel with و, so the print is four و-joined clauses separated by commas, and the boundaries belong at 279/289/299, not inside the labels. Splitting the first alone would break the parallelism the author built. A CORRECTION TO MY OWN LAW 0, which governed the three declines above: the 5:1 figure describes my BIAS, not the scoring loss. Under F1 a false cut costs roughly what a miss costs, so “cut at a coin flip” means cut at 0.5, not cut at 0.3. I applied that ceiling at 271, at 145–147, at 167, and at 322 (ومن أعمال كورساكوف الشهيرة | افتتاحية عيد الفصح الروسي — a colon is possible, but an inverted nominal sentence needs none). SITE 326 (الروسي | وعاش كورساكوف). CUT, hi. LAW 1 in its cleanest form: و followed by a finite verb that RE-NAMES its subject with a full explicit NP (كورساكوف rather than a pronoun) is the strongest new-sentence signal in the corpus — an author who repeats the proper name has started a new sentence. The same signal licensed the cut at 218. Recording a process note against myself: I argued this site correctly and then dropped it when transcribing my boundary list, and only caught it by rendering the segments back out and seeing a 19-token closing unit against a 7.6 mean. Segment-length review after committing is now part of my procedure, not an optional check. SITES 312 AND 333 (عندما, حتى). NOT cut. LAW 4: a subordinate clause that FOLLOWS its main clause belongs to it — the بعد أن error of batch 1.
